reason: One functional case per reproduction step (v2 matching/lower/upper case, v1 by-name lower case), one boundary case keeping starts-with semantics (name=Backpack returns 0), and three regression cases for paging, brand filter and type filter combined with a case-insensitive name.

items.title: v2 search with name=Explorer (matching case) returns the four Explorer items
covers: Expected: step 1 result is the reference (4 items, count 4)
items.reason: Step 1 is the reference the other steps are compared with, and the fix must not break the search that worked before. Functional layer: the endpoint, EF query and real Postgres are exercised in-process, which is where the name comparison happens; no UI is involved.

items.title: v2 search with name=explorer (all lower case) returns the same four Explorer items
covers: Expected: step 2 returns the same four items with count 4
items.reason: This is the reported defect: a lower-case search returned count 0. It is the core regression case. Functional layer because the defect lives in the query translated to Postgres, so an in-memory unit test would not prove the database comparison.

items.title: v2 search with name=EXPLORER (all upper case) returns the same four Explorer items
covers: Expected: step 3 returns the same four items with count 4
items.reason: The ticket names upper-case search text separately from lower case; a fix that only lower-cases the stored name (or only the input) would pass TC-BUG-43-02 but fail here. Same layer reasoning as TC-BUG-43-02.

items.title: v1 GET /items/by/explorer returns the same four Explorer items
covers: Expected: step 4 (v1 /items/by/{name}) returns the same four items with count 4
items.reason: The v1 by-name route is a separate public endpoint in the ticket's reproduction; it must be fixed too, not only the v2 query parameter. Functional layer to hit the real v1 route with its `minlength(1)` constraint and the real database.

items.title: v2 search with name=Backpack returns no items (match stays anchored at the start of the name)
covers: Expected: the name still matches from the start of the item's name (name=Backpack returns no items)
items.reason: The ticket keeps starts-with semantics; a fix that switched to a contains match (for example `ILIKE '%x%'`) would make the search case-insensitive but wrongly return the many items whose names end in "Backpack". This is the boundary of the change. Functional layer for the real database query.

items.title: Paging applies to a lower-case name search: second page of size 2 holds the last two Explorer items
items.reason: The ticket says paging is unchanged. The total `count` must stay the full match count (4) while `data` holds only the requested page, in name order; a fix that counted or paged a different query would break this. Functional layer because count and Skip/Take run against the database.

items.title: Brand filter still narrows a lower-case name search to the B&R Explorer items
covers: Expected: the brand filter is unchanged
items.reason: The ticket says the brand filter is unchanged; the name and brand predicates must still combine (AND). Two of the four Explorer items are B&R, so the filter's effect is observable. Functional layer for the combined database query.

items.title: Type filter still narrows an upper-case name search to the one Footwear Explorer item
covers: Expected: the type filter is unchanged
items.reason: The ticket says the type filter is unchanged; the name and type predicates must still combine. Only one Explorer item is Footwear, so the filter's effect is observable. Separate from the brand case because the two filters are separate predicates. Functional layer for the combined database query.
